title: MIRAGE: Quantum Circuit Decomposition and Routing Collaborative Design Using Mirror Gates
problem: Building efficient large-scale quantum computers requires transpilation to ensure gates operate on physically connected qubits while minimizing SWAP gates and efficiently decomposing into native basis gates.
motivation: Minimizing circuit depth and maximizing execution fidelity are critical for practical quantum computing with limited qubit connectivity and noisy hardware.
method: MIRAGE reduces quantum circuit overhead on real hardware by using mirror gates—quantum gates that produce symmetric operations when outputs are reversed. A greedy algorithm selectively substitutes mirror gates at adjustable aggression levels, exploiting √iSWAP's efficient decomposition into native gates (the quantum operations the hardware can run) to simultaneously reduce SWAP routing (expensive operations between physically connected qubits) and improve gate decomposition. The method analyzes hardware fault rates to balance circuit execution speed (circuit depth) against decomposition accuracy.
key_novelty: Mirror gates simultaneously reduce SWAP operations, improve gate decomposition, and minimize circuit depth—rather than optimizing for SWAP count alone.
contributions: Mirror gate approach enabling collaborative circuit decomposition and routing optimization
Greedy substitution algorithm with configurable aggression levels for mirror gate selection
Comprehensive fault rate analysis trading circuit depth against decomposition accuracy for √iSWAP and 4√SWAP
Demonstration of 29.6% circuit depth reduction and 59.9% SWAP elimination on iSWAP systems with 28% infidelity improvement

metrics.speedup: 29.6% circuit depth reduction on iSWAP systems
metrics.accuracy: 28% relative infidelity reduction for iSWAP, 21% for CNOT, 19% for SYC

primary_theme: quantum circuit optimization via mirror gates
